# yocto

> yocto is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) inversion-of-control (IoC) / dependency injection container for .NET 10 from MILL5. It is a drop-in IServiceProvider for Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection and ASP.NET Core (passes all 143 tests in Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Specification.Tests 10.0), and adds child containers, per-thread and pooled lifetimes, modules, and build-time validation in about 1,200 lines of C# (excluding comments). Install with `dotnet add package yocto`. Built by Microsoft MVP Richard Crane at MILL5.

Key facts:
- NuGet: yocto (core), yocto.Wpf (XAML markup extension) — version {{ site.version }}
- Target: net10.0 (yocto 1.x/2.x for .NET Framework, .NET Standard, and Xamarin are no longer maintained)
- Namespace: Yocto (yocto.Wpf: Yocto.Wpf)
- Dependency: Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions only
- Lifetimes: Multiple (transient, default), Singleton (optionally eager), Scoped, PerThread, Pooled, Instance (never disposed), custom via Lifetimes.Register
- Features: keyed services ([FromKeyedServices], [ServiceKey], KeyedService.AnyKey), open generics, IEnumerable<T>, child containers, IServiceScopeFactory, IAsyncDisposable, Validate() for missing/circular/captive dependencies, IModule, assembly registration, Application.Current ambient container, Native AOT annotations
- ASP.NET Core: builder.Host.UseServiceProviderFactory(new YoctoServiceProviderFactory())
- Source: https://github.com/MILL5/yocto
- Website: {{ '/' | absolute_url }}
- License: Apache 2.0 (free, open source)
- NuGet downloads: 43K+
- Author: Richard Crane (Microsoft MVP, Founder of MILL5) — https://mvp.microsoft.com/en-US/MVP/profile/10ce0bc0-7536-43f6-b28c-e9601a4a0d0d
- Publisher: MILL5, LLC — https://mill5.com (Boston-based Microsoft Gold Partner)
- Podcast: Inventing Fire with AI — https://inventingfirewith.ai
- Support: rich@mill5.com

## Quick start

```csharp
using Yocto;

using var container = new Container();
container.RegisterSingleton<IClock, SystemClock>();
container.Register<IGreeter, Greeter>();   // Greeter(IClock clock) is constructor-injected
container.Validate();
var greeter = container.Resolve<IGreeter>();
```
